newsitem.title: GERMANY: Military meeting on Zaire relief set for Friday.
newsitem.headline: Military meeting on Zaire relief set for Friday.

text.p: A meeting of military leaders from nations expected to send troops on a relief mission to Rwanda and Zaire will take place on Friday, the Canadian military said on Thursday.

The meeting is to be held at the U.S. European Command in Stuttgart, which is the headquarters for U.S. operations in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. It will be chaired by Canada, which is coordinating efforts to establish the multinational force.
A Canadian Forces spokesman in Stuttgart said the meeting would begin at 1000 GMT at Kelly Barracks and that a news conference was expected to be held after the meeting.
"In general terms, the meeting will be held to determine and decide on the general scope of the mission," Canadian Navy Reserve Lieutenant Charles Brown told Reuters.

Military leaders from several nations including the United States, France, Britain and Canada were expected to attend the meeting, which was called to review plans for the mission after hundreds of thousands of refugees began returning to Rwanda.
Canada said on Wednesday at the United Nations that most nations involved in the humanitarian crisis in Africa believed a military force was still needed to deliver aid to refugees.
